messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm seeing a tight cohort of GPUs in us-west2 (rack-11) with thermal fuse trips + Xid 31 after ~10-15m warmup. Started at ~06:10 UTC. Impact: ~12 GPUs out (~4% of west2 pool.

jon: Can you paste the alert/graph?

ops-bot: ALERT: ECC error rate spike detected in us-west2/gpu-pool-3. Probe: 2030012345. Graph: https://telemetry.internal/redwood/alerts/2030012345

maria: Logs/snip from r11-05 dmesg and nvidia-smi: 
```
[  645.123456] NVRM: Xid (31): Deep GPU exception on GPU 0
GPU 0: Power: 250W, Temp: 92C, thermal_policy: THRM_FUSE
# nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,power.draw,utilization.gpu --format=csv
0, A5000, 92, 249.8 W, 98 %
```

sara: Is it localized to a vendor batch or spread across racks?

maria: Mostly r11-03..r11-08, same procurement batch (vendor X, lot 2023-07). Not seeing the same pattern in r10 or r12.

liam: Can we drain those nodes and shift workloads? How bad is capacity hit for prod?

devon: If we evict those 6 hosts (12 gpus) we'll lose ~3.2% of overall prod GPU capacity in us-west2 — currently 150 queued jobs would be delayed. We can route some jobs to us-west1 reserved capacity but that'll cost.

jon: Let's start with an ordered plan: 1) immediate drain of the affected hosts, 2) apply temporary power cap to remaining rack-11 nodes to avoid further trips, 3) mark drained GPUs for RMA and replacement, 4) enable cross-region failover to us-west1 reserved pool. Opinions?

sara: +1 to drain. Also run a targeted health-scan so we don't miss intermittent failures: `health-scan --nodes r11-03..r11-08 --deep --log`

maria: ran health-scan, results attached (short): persistent ECC/Xid after reboot on 9/12 GPUs in the cohort; thermal sensors 0/1/2 showing +8C bias vs baseline.

drain-bot: drain-bot: Initiating drain for nodes r11-03 r11-04 r11-05 r11-06 r11-07 r11-08 (owner: @jon). Expected completion ~20m.

liam: As a soft mitigation, I'll push power cap 200W to all remaining rack-11 GPUs — throughput drop ~6-9% but should reduce thermal stress. Patching now.

devon: Cost/tradeoff note: routing queued jobs to us-west1 reserved ramps cost by $2.1k/day at current utilization. Alternatively we can spin up transient capacity in us-west3 (cheaper but ~10-15m provisioning lag). Which do we prefer?

jon: For immediate safety, use reserved failover in us-west1 for latency-sensitive routes; fallback noncritical to us-west3 spot pools. We'll accept the $2.1k/day until RMAs complete.

hw-team: ack — we'll schedule RMA for those hosts, inventory says spares available. ETA for swaps: 48-72h depending on vendor queue.

maria: I'll open an incident ticket and start a postmortem doc with initial timeline + affected customer surfaces.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Created incident INC-2030-112 (link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2030-112) — assigned to eng-infra and hw-team.

jon: Action owners: @hw-team (RMA + replace), @liam (power cap + verify thermal rollback), @devon (routing + cost temporary), @maria (incident + PM), @sara (follow-up health scans). Check-in in 2h or earlier if more trips.

maria: Note: after power cap pushed, one host reported degraded perf but no new Xid events in 25m. Will keep monitoring. :thumbsup:

devon: I'll post cost delta summary to #finance later today.

jon: Thanks team — keep this thread for updates only. If anything changes escalate to pager. :rotating_light:
